content.content:
########## conf/v2_linux_ae350_none.lua ##########
-- Linux on a -M none platform: the ae350 board's peripherals as SystemC
-- modules. CPUs, PLIC, PLICSW (IPIs), PLMT (timer), the console 16550,
-- the SMU and the small APB blocks are QEMU device models wrapped one per
-- module; DRAM, the boot ROM, the device-tree ROM, NOR and L2C are
-- gs_memory; the loader places u-boot-spl (ELF), the FIT image, the dtb
-- and the reset vector. Blocks the ae350 board itself leaves unimplemented
-- (SMC, SPI, GPIO, I2C, LCD, SND, MAC, SD) are zero-reading memory so the
-- kernel's probes fail cleanly instead of faulting.
--
-- The console is uart2 (0xf0300000, ttyS0 in the dtb); its chardev is a
-- telnet server so the boot can be driven from a second terminal:
--     telnet 127.0.0.1 43219
-- Change uart2.chardev to "stdio" for an interactive run.
local NUM_CPUS = 4
local SPL_ENTRY = 0x800000        -- readelf -h images/u-boot-spl
local DTB_ADDR = 0xf2000000       -- ae350 DTROM
local ITB_ADDR = 0x10000000       -- where the SPL expects linux.itb

platform = {
    moduletype = "Container",
    quantum_ns = 1000000,

    router = { moduletype = "router" },

    -- Memories
    dram = {
        moduletype = "gs_memory",
        target_socket = { address = 0x00000000, size = 0x80000000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" },
    },
    mrom = {
        moduletype = "gs_memory",
        target_socket = { address = 0x80000000, size = 0x8000000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" },
    },
    nor = {
        moduletype = "gs_memory",
        target_socket = { address = 0x88000000, size = 0x4000000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" },
    },
    l2c = {
        moduletype = "gs_memory",
        target_socket = { address = 0xe0500000, size = 0x100000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" },
    },
    dtrom = {
        moduletype = "gs_memory",
        target_socket = { address = 0xf2000000, size = 0x100000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" },
    },
    -- Unimplemented APB/AXI blocks (read as zero, writes ignored)
    unimpl_mac  = { moduletype = "gs_memory", target_socket = { address = 0xe0100000, size = 0x100000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" } },
    unimpl_lcd  = { moduletype = "gs_memory", target_socket = { address = 0xe0200000, size = 0x100000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" } },
    unimpl_smc  = { moduletype = "gs_memory", target_socket = { address = 0xe0400000, size = 0x100000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" } },
    unimpl_gpio = { moduletype = "gs_memory", target_socket = { address = 0xf0700000, size = 0x100000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" } },
    unimpl_i2c  = { moduletype = "gs_memory", target_socket = { address = 0xf0a00000, size = 0x100000, bind = "&router.initiator_socket" } },

Now the cause is located precisely, and it is **not** the mechanism:

```
[main  ] it=7 t=7 ns d=21 ticks=7 seen=7   <- sc_start(1ns) returns BEFORE the t=7ns edge
[edge  ] t=7 ns d=22 ticks->8
THREAD wakes t=7 ns d=22 base=8            <- woke in the SAME delta, after that edge
[thread] it=1 t=8 ns d=24 ticks=8 seen=0   <- so its baseline was one edge ahead
```

Per-iteration alignment is **identical** for `sc_start(period)` and `wait(period)` — both observe one edge behind. The gap was my test's mid-simulation handoff sampling its baseline one edge late. Fix: let the thread phase run from `t=0`, where both are aligned by construction.

      : ahb_{ahb}, cycle_{cycle}
  {}""",
"""  // `clock` decides how a busy transaction is waited out: vsim's own binary
  // owns the SystemC kernel and starts it, while under FastSim the kernel owns
  // vsim and this runs inside a process that must yield instead.
  SystemCDmiBus(ahb_manager& ahb, const sc_core::sc_time& cycle,
                CycleClock& clock)
      : ahb_{ahb}, cycle_{cycle}, clock_{clock}
  {}""",1)
s=s.replace("    while (ahb_.txn.is_busy()) sc_core::sc_start(cycle_);",
            "    while (ahb_.txn.is_busy()) clock_.advance(cycle_);",1)
s=s.replace("""  ahb_manager& ahb_;
  sc_core::sc_time cycle_;""",
"""  ahb_manager& ahb_;
  sc_core::sc_time cycle_;
  CycleClock& clock_;""",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

# ---- 2. Simulator: own a default clock, let a wrapper replace it ------------
p='src/simulator.hpp'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('#include "platform/memory_map.h"\n#include "platform/platform.hpp"',
            '#include "platform/cycle_clock.hpp"\n#include "platform/memory_map.h"\n#include "platform/platform.hpp"',1)

s=s.replace("""private:
  // debug
  jtag_dtm& dtm;""",
"""private:
  // How the per-cycle loop advances the kernel. Declared before every user so
  // member init order is safe. Default: this process owns the kernel.
  ScStartClock own_cycle_clock_;
  CycleClock* cycle_clock_ = &own_cycle_clock_;

  // debug
  jtag_dtm& dtm;""",1)

# public accessors, placed at the existing `public:` before ContextManager
s=s.replace("""public:
  ContextManager<CPU> context_config;""",
"""public:
  // Under FastSim the kernel owns this simulator: sc_start() is called once by
  // FastSim's sc_main, so the loop below runs inside an SC_THREAD and must
  // yield rather than start the kernel. Set this before reset()/run().
  void set_cycle_clock(CycleClock& clock) { cycle_clock_ = &clock; }
  auto cycle_clock() -> CycleClock& { return *cycle_clock_; }

  ContextManager<CPU> context_config;""",1)

# the run loop
assert s.count("      sc_core::sc_start(platform.clk.period());")==1
s=s.replace("      sc_core::sc_start(platform.clk.period());",
            "      cycle_clock_->advance(platform.clk.period());",1)

# all DMI bus constructions
n=s.count("bus{platform.dmi, platform.clk.period()};")
assert n==2, n
s=s.replace("bus{platform.dmi, platform.clk.period()};",
            "bus{platform.dmi, platform.clk.period(), *cycle_clock_};")
s=s.replace("""                            PLATFORM::dmi_data_width>>(platform.dmi,
                                                       platform.clk.period());""",
"""                            PLATFORM::dmi_data_width>>(platform.dmi,
                                                       platform.clk.period(),
                                                       *cycle_clock_);""",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

# ---- 3. main.cpp: end-of-elaboration goes through the same clock -----------
p='src/main.cpp'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""    // End of elaboration
    sc_core::sc_start(sc_core::SC_ZERO_TIME);""",
"""    // End of elaboration. Routed through the simulator's clock so this file
    // holds no mechanism of its own: under FastSim the equivalent settling step
    // is a delta inside the kernel, not a call that starts it.
    sim.cycle_clock().advance(sc_core::SC_ZERO_TIME);""",1)

# ##############################################################################
# Per-CPU targets
# ##############################################################################

# Wires a per-CPU executable up with the include paths, compile/link options,
# verilated CPU library, and aceasim glue. Relies on per-CPU variables set
# inside the foreach loop below (CPU_NAME, CPU_UPPER, RTL, OBJ_SC_DIR,
# _aceasim_lib, _stub_aceasim_lib).
macro(vsim_add_cpu_executable _target _source)
  add_executable(${_target} ${ARGN} ${_source})
  target_include_directories(${_target} SYSTEM PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
  )
  target_include_directories(${_target} PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi"
  )
  target_compile_options(${_target} PRIVATE ${VSIM_COMPILE_FLAGS})
  target_compile_definitions(${_target} PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_COMPILE_DEFS}
    VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}
  )
  target_link_options(${_target} PRIVATE ${VSIM_LINK_FLAGS})
  target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
    ${VSIM_DEP_LIBS}
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    ${VSIM_LINK_LIBS}
  )
  if(_aceasim_lib)
    target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE
      -Wl,--whole-archive
      "${_aceasim_lib}"
      -Wl,--no-whole-archive
    )
  endif()
  if(_stub_aceasim_lib)
    target_link_options(${_target} PRIVATE
      "-Wl,--undefined=get_libaceasim_version")
    target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE "${_stub_aceasim_lib}")
  endif()
  add_dependencies(${_target} deps generate_headers)
  if(NOT VSIM_NO_VERILATOR)
    add_dependencies(${_target} verilated_${CPU_NAME})
  endif()
endmacro()

foreach(CPU_NAME IN LISTS VSIM_CPU_LIST)
  string(TOUPPER "${CPU_NAME}" CPU_UPPER)
  string(TOLOWER "${CPU_NAME}" CPU_LOWER)

  set(RTL "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_RTL_PACKAGE}")
  set(LIBACEASIM_PATH "${VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER}_LIBACEASIM_PATH}")
  set(OBJ_SC_DIR "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/V${CPU_NAME}/obj_sc")

  # Resolve libaceasim

  # _aceasim_lib: user's libaceasim.a generated from COPILOT.
  # _stub_aceasim_lib: stubs-built libaceasim.a, always linked to sim_<cpu> when
  # given a string.
  # The stubs provide all required four DPI-C symbols (ace, ace_pre_dec, vace, vace_dec)
  # as defaults in case _aceasim_lib doesn't include any of them. This can happen
  # when ACE file only has ACE-Scalar or ACE-RVV instructions, so that COPILOT
  # doesn't generate the other types of DPI-C modules.
  #
  if(LIBACEASIM_PATH AND NOT LIBACEASIM_PATH MATCHES "^stubs")
    set(_aceasim_lib "${LIBACEASIM_PATH}")
  endif()

  if(LIBACEASIM_PATH)
    set(_stub_aceasim_lib "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libaceasim.a")
  else()
    set(_stub_aceasim_lib "")
    set(_aceasim_lib "")
  endif()

  # Verilator custom commands (unless --no-verilator)
  if(NOT VSIM_NO_VERILATOR)
    vsim_add_verilated_cpu("${CPU_NAME}")
  endif()

  vsim_add_cpu_executable(sim_${CPU_NAME} src/main.cpp)
  list(APPEND ALL_SIM_TARGETS sim_${CPU_NAME})
endforeach()

# ##############################################################################

########## gs_create_dymod macro ##########
macro(gs_systemc)
    install_systemc()
    install_systemc_dependencies()
    configure_systemc()
endmacro()
# ##############################################################################

macro(gs_create_dymod MODULE_NAME)
  file(GLOB_RECURSE SOURCE_COMPONENT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cc")

  add_library(${MODULE_NAME} SHARED
              ${SOURCE_COMPONENT})

  # Define where to install the dynamic library during building
  set_target_properties(${MODULE_NAME} PROPERTIES
                        LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})

  # Avoid to have the "lib" prefix on the name of the library
  set_target_properties(${MODULE_NAME} PROPERTIES PREFIX "")

  if ( TARGET_LIBS )
    add_dependencies(${MODULE_NAME} ${TARGET_LIBS})
    target_link_libraries(${MODULE_NAME} PUBLIC
        ${TARGET_LIBS}
    )
  endif()

  foreach(T IN LISTS TARGET_LIBS)
    target_include_directories(
      ${MODULE_NAME} PUBLIC
      $<TARGET_PROPERTY:${T},INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>
    )
  endforeach()

  target_include_directories(
    ${MODULE_NAME} PUBLIC
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
    $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}>
  )

  install(
    TARGETS ${MODULE_NAME}
    # we export the ${MODULE_NAME}, like that we can use ${MODULE_NAME} with qqvp.
    EXPORT qqvpTargets
    LIBRARY DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
            COMPONENT "${LIBRARY_NAME}_Runtime"
            NAMELINK_COMPONENT "${LIBRARY_NAME}_Development"
  )

endmacro()

# ##############################################################################
# ----- LUA
# ##############################################################################
macro(build_lua)
  if (lua_ADDED)
      # lua has no CMake support, so we create our own target
      FILE(GLOB lua_sources ${lua_SOURCE_DIR}/*.c)
      list(REMOVE_ITEM lua_sources "${lua_SOURCE_DIR}/lua.c" "${lua_SOURCE_DIR}/luac.c" "${lua_SOURCE_DIR}/ltests.c" "${lua_SOURCE_DIR}/onelua.c")
      add_library(lua SHARED ${lua_sources})
      target_compile_definitions(lua PRIVATE LUA_USE_POSIX)
      target_include_directories(lua PUBLIC $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${lua_SOURCE_DIR}>)
      target_compile_definitions(${PROJECT_NAME} INTERFACE HAS_LUA)
      target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PUBLIC lua)
      list(APPEND TARGET_LIBS "lua")
      install(TARGETS lua EXPORT ${PROJECT_NAME}Targets)
  endif()
endmacro()

#! /bin/bash

set -o pipefail

check_build_type() {
    local build_type="$1"

    case "$build_type" in
        "Debug" | "Release" | "RelWithDebInfo" | "MinSizeRel" | "")
            return 0
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Invalid: BUILD_TYPE='$build_type' is not a recognized standard CMake build type." >&2
            echo "Supported values: Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo, MinSizeRel, or empty string" >&2
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
}

#This function will truncate buildlog file, and then add message to it
check_previous_build_status() {
    local buildlog="$1"
    local buildtype="$2"
    local buildace="$3"
    local systemc_prefix="$4"
    shift 4
    local cmake_opts=("$@")

    local pre_buildace=0
    local log_buildtype=`grep "Build type is " $buildlog | head -n 1 | cut -d ' ' -f 4`
    if [ "$buildtype" != "$log_buildtype" ]; then
        echo "Different build type (pre: $log_buildtype, curr: $buildtype)" | tee $buildlog
        return 1
    fi

    local log_buildace=`grep "ACE feature is " $buildlog | head -n 1 | cut -d ' ' -f 4`
    if [ "$log_buildace" == "enabled" ]; then
        pre_buildace=1
    fi

    if [ "$buildace" != "$pre_buildace" ]; then
        echo "Different Build ACE (pre: $pre_buildace, curr: $buildace)" | tee $buildlog
        return 1
    fi

    local log_systemc=`grep "SystemC Prefix is " $buildlog | head -n 1 | cut -d ' ' -f 4`
    if [ "$systemc_prefix" != "$log_systemc" ]; then
        echo "Different SystemC Prefix (pre: $log_systemc, curr: $systemc_prefix)" | tee $buildlog
        return 1
    fi

    local log_cmake_opts=`grep "Custom CMake options: " $buildlog | head -n 1 | sed 's/Custom CMake options: //'`
    if [ "${cmake_opts[*]}" != "$log_cmake_opts" ]; then
        echo "Different Custom CMake options (pre: $log_cmake_opts, curr: ${cmake_opts[*]})" | tee $buildlog
        return 1
    fi

    echo "Checking previous build status done" | tee $buildlog
    return 0
}

content.text: Writing the RED acceptance test for S1:

input.command:
cd /home/nick/work/andesim
cat > tests/drivers/cycle_mode_on_lua.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# S1 acceptance: cycle mode must give the SAME number when FastSim owns the
# SystemC kernel as it does when vsim's own binary owns it.
#
# Today vsim drives the kernel itself: its run loop calls sc_start(period) once
# per cycle from sc_main. Under FastSim, sc_main belongs to FastSim -- it calls
# sc_start() once and everything else lives inside the kernel. That inversion
# is the whole of S1, and the only honest test of it is the product: README
# line 8 sells one number, so that number must not move.
#
# Method: run the same ELF twice and require the two counts to be equal.
#   1. vsim standalone            -- "<N> cycles simulated"
#   2. FastSim + a Lua platform   -- the same line, from VsimCore
# Both numbers come from Simulator::get_cycles(), so any difference is the
# inversion changing behaviour, which is exactly what must not happen.
#
# Skips (77) rather than fails when a binary or the Lua platform is absent: an
# environment without a FastSim build has nothing to say about S1.
set -uo pipefail

NAME=cycle_mode_on_lua
ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_matmul}"
ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$ROOT/tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-300}"

skip() { echo "[skip] $NAME: $*"; exit 77; }
fail() { echo "FAIL[$NAME]: $*"; exit 1; }

# -- what this test needs -----------------------------------------------------
VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
[ -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]   || skip "vsim engine not built: $VSIM_BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ]        || skip "fixture ELF not built: $ELF"
[ -n "${FASTSIM_BIN:-}" ] || skip "FASTSIM_BIN unset (path to multi_arch_toplevel)"
[ -x "${FASTSIM_BIN}" ]   || skip "FastSim not built: $FASTSIM_BIN"

[ -f "${VSIM_CYCLE_LUA}" ]   || skip "Lua platform missing: $VSIM_CYCLE_LUA"

# Lift the one number vsim reports. Shared by both legs on purpose: if the two
# legs scraped differently, a formatting change could hide a real move.
cycles_from() {
  sed -nE 's/.*[^0-9]([0-9]+) cycles simulated.*/\1/p' | tail -1
}

# -- leg 1: vsim owns the kernel (today) --------------------------------------
STANDALONE_OUT=$(timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$ELF" 2>&1)
STANDALONE_RC=$?
STANDALONE=$(printf '%s\n' "$STANDALONE_OUT" | cycles_from)
[ -n "$STANDALONE" ] || fail "vsim standalone reported no cycle count (rc=$STANDALONE_RC)
$(printf '%s\n' "$STANDALONE_OUT" | tail -5)"

# -- leg 2: FastSim owns the kernel (S1) --------------------------------------
# The ELF reaches VsimCore as a CCI preset rather than a CLI flag, because
# under FastSim the platform file is the interface.
HOSTED_OUT=$(timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$FASTSIM_BIN" \
  --gs_luafile "$VSIM_CYCLE_LUA" \
  -p "platform.vsim.elf_file=\"$ELF\"" 2>&1)
HOSTED_RC=$?
HOSTED=$(printf '%s\n' "$HOSTED_OUT" | cycles_from)
[ -n "$HOSTED" ] || fail "FastSim-hosted run reported no cycle count (rc=$HOSTED_RC)
$(printf '%s\n' "$HOSTED_OUT" | tail -15)"

# -- the contract -------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$STANDALONE" != "$HOSTED" ]; then
  fail "cycle count moved when FastSim took the kernel:
  vsim standalone (sc_start per cycle): $STANDALONE
  FastSim + Lua   (wait per cycle):     $HOSTED
  moved by $((HOSTED - STANDALONE)) cycles on fixture $FIXTURE"
fi

echo "[$NAME] PASS: $FIXTURE = $STANDALONE cycles, both ways"
EOF

input.command:
cd /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim
python3 - <<'PY'
p='CMakeLists.txt'
s=open(p).read()

macro = r'''
# Wires a per-CPU FastSim module (integration plan S1): the same Verilated core
# and Simulator as sim_<cpu>, packaged so FastSim's ModuleFactory can dlopen it
# and a Lua platform file can name it.
#
# Guarded by FASTSIM_DIR because it needs the greenlib-v2 headers that carry
# GSC_MODULE_REGISTER_C; with FASTSIM_DIR unset, vsim builds exactly as before.
#
# The library deliberately does NOT link libsystemc.a. One process may hold one
# SystemC kernel, and that kernel belongs to the FastSim executable that loads
# this module; linking a second copy in here would give the module its own
# scheduler and its own simulation time. The symbols resolve at dlopen against
# the host executable, which CMake links with -rdynamic.
macro(vsim_add_fastsim_module _target)
  add_library(${_target} SHARED src/fastsim/vsim_core.cc)
  # ModuleFactory dlopens "<name>.so", so no "lib" prefix.
  set_target_properties(${_target} PROPERTIES PREFIX "")
  target_include_directories(${_target} SYSTEM PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    # greenlib-v2 carries GSC_MODULE_REGISTER_C; scp/report.h is its only
    # non-standard dependency and pulls no logging library of its own.
    "${FASTSIM_DIR}/libs/greenlib-v2/common/include"
    "${FASTSIM_DIR}/libs/systemc-common-practices/report/include"
  )
  target_include_directories(${_target} PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src"
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi")
  target_compile_options(${_target} PRIVATE ${VSIM_COMPILE_FLAGS})
  target_compile_definitions(${_target} PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_COMPILE_DEFS}
    VSIM_CPU_${CPU_UPPER})
  target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/V${RTL}__ALL.a"
    "${DEPS_DIR}/fmt/lib/libfmt.a"
    "${DEPS_DIR}/spdlog/lib/libspdlog.a"
    "${DEPS_DIR}/lief/lib/libLIEF.a"
    "${DEPS_DIR}/andes_clarity/lib/libdatabase_handler.a"
    "${DEPS_DIR}/systemc-cci/lib/libcci.a"
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}/libverilated.a"
    ${VSIM_LINK_LIBS}
  )
  # The host executable supplies SystemC; leaving it out is the point, so do
  # not let the linker fail the library for those symbols.
  target_link_options(${_target} PRIVATE "-Wl,--unresolved-symbols=ignore-all")
  if(_aceasim_lib)
    target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE
      -Wl,--whole-archive "${_aceasim_lib}" -Wl,--no-whole-archive)
  endif()
  if(_stub_aceasim_lib)
    target_link_libraries(${_target} PRIVATE "${_stub_aceasim_lib}")
  endif()
  add_dependencies(${_target} deps generate_headers)
  if(NOT VSIM_NO_VERILATOR)
    add_dependencies(${_target} verilated_${CPU_NAME})
  endif()
endmacro()

'''

anchor = "foreach(CPU_NAME IN LISTS VSIM_CPU_LIST)"

  # S1: the same core as a FastSim module. One moduletype name for every

  if(FASTSIM_DIR)

input.command:
cd /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim
mkdir -p conf
cat > conf/andesim_cycle.lua.in <<'EOF'
-- AndeSim cycle mode as a FastSim platform (integration plan S1).
--
-- Today `andesim run --mode cycle` spawns a vsim binary and reads one number
-- off its output. The binary owns the SystemC kernel: its run loop calls
-- sc_start once per clock period. This file is the same run with the ownership
-- inverted -- FastSim's sc_main loads it, calls sc_start() once, and VsimCore
-- steps the core from inside the kernel instead.
--
-- What is NOT here is the point of the staging. Cycle mode is the RTL from
-- reset, so it needs no QEMU, no router and no shared devices: vsim keeps its
-- own memory, UART, SMU and SimControl exactly as it has them. Sharing one
-- device set is S2, and that is when a router appears below.
--
-- elf_file is left empty on purpose. The guest program is the one thing that
-- changes per run, so the CLI passes it:
--   multi_arch_toplevel --gs_luafile andesim_cycle.lua \
--     -p 'platform.vsim.elf_file="/path/to/kernel.elf"'

platform = {
    moduletype = "Container",

    vsim = {
        moduletype = "VsimCore",
        -- ModuleFactory appends ".so". One moduletype name serves every
        -- engine; this path is what selects which engine build is loaded,
        -- so a second engine is another line, not another class.
        dylib_path = "@VSIM_CORE_DYLIB_STEM@",

        elf_file = "",

        -- Wait states SimpleMemory reports to the core. 1 is vsim's own
        -- default (--mem-latency). Every recorded cycle count in andesim's
        -- tests/baseline/kernel_cycles.tsv was measured at this value, so
        -- changing it is a decision to re-record, not a tuning knob.
        mem_latency = 1,

        -- 0 means no cycle budget, matching the standalone engine.
        max_cycles = 0,
    },
}
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
p='CMakeLists.txt'
s=open(p).read()
old = """  # S1: the same core as a FastSim module. One moduletype name for every
  # engine; a Lua platform picks the engine with dylib_path.
  if(FASTSIM_DIR)
    vsim_add_fastsim_module(VsimCore_${CPU_NAME})
    list(APPEND ALL_FASTSIM_MODULES VsimCore_${CPU_NAME})
  endif()"""
new = """  # S1: the same core as a FastSim module. One moduletype name for every
  # engine; a Lua platform picks the engine with dylib_path.
  if(FASTSIM_DIR)
    vsim_add_fastsim_module(VsimCore_${CPU_NAME})
    list(APPEND ALL_FASTSIM_MODULES VsimCore_${CPU_NAME})
    # Generated rather than checked in: the .so path is a build-tree fact, and
    # a stale hand-written one silently loads the wrong engine.
    set(VSIM_CORE_DYLIB_STEM "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/VsimCore_${CPU_NAME}")

  endif()"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new,1)

content.text:
Root cause found, and it's a real collision — not a scope problem:

```
libstdc++ <semaphore> → bits/semaphore_base.h:45 → #include <semaphore.h>
   ... resolves to /fastsim/libs/greenlib-v2/common/include/semaphore.h
```

greenlib-v2 ships a `semaphore.h` that **shadows the POSIX header**, and Verilator's `verilated.h` includes `<thread>`. The fix is to search greenlib *after* the system dirs (`-idirafter`), so POSIX wins but `<cciutils.h>` is still found:

input.command:
cd /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim
python3 - <<'PY'
p='CMakeLists.txt'
s=open(p).read()
old = '''  target_include_directories(${_target} SYSTEM PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    # greenlib-v2 carries GSC_MODULE_REGISTER_C; scp/report.h is its only
    # non-standard dependency and pulls no logging library of its own.
    "${FASTSIM_DIR}/libs/greenlib-v2/common/include"
    "${FASTSIM_DIR}/libs/systemc-common-practices/report/include"
  )'''
new = '''  target_include_directories(${_target} SYSTEM PRIVATE
    ${VSIM_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    "${OBJ_SC_DIR}"
    "${FASTSIM_DIR}/libs/systemc-common-practices/report/include"
  )
  # greenlib-v2's include dir goes AFTER the standard system directories, not
  # before them, and that is not a preference.
  #
  # greenlib ships common/include/semaphore.h -- a C++ class, not the POSIX
  # header of that name. Verilator's verilated.h includes <thread>, libstdc++'s
  # <thread> reaches <semaphore>, and <bits/semaphore_base.h> then asks for
  # <semaphore.h>. With greenlib ahead of libc, that request lands on greenlib's
  # file and libstdc++ fails to compile. -idirafter puts libc's header first
  # while still finding <cciutils.h> and <module_factory_registery.h>, which
  # exist nowhere else. The collision only shows up here because this is the
  # first thing to combine Verilator with greenlib in one translation unit.
  target_compile_options(${_target} PRIVATE
    "SHELL:-idirafter ${FASTSIM_DIR}/libs/greenlib-v2/common/include")'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("patched with -idirafter")
PY

content.text: No CLI param support — the test must compose a Lua. Let me rewrite it to layer overrides over the generated platform:

input.command:
cd /home/nick/work/andesim
rm -f tests/drivers/cycle_mode_on_lua.sh
cat > tests/drivers/cycle_mode_on_lua.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# S1 acceptance: cycle mode must give the SAME number when FastSim owns the
# SystemC kernel as it does when vsim's own binary owns it.
#
# Today vsim drives the kernel itself: its run loop calls sc_start(period) once
# per cycle from sc_main. Under FastSim, sc_main belongs to FastSim -- it calls
# sc_start() once and everything else lives inside the kernel. That inversion
# is the whole of S1, and the only honest test of it is the product: README
# line 8 sells one number, so that number must not move.
#
# Method: run the same ELF twice and require the two counts to be equal.
#   1. vsim standalone           -- "<N> cycles simulated"
#   2. FastSim + a Lua platform  -- the same line, from VsimCore
# Both numbers come from Simulator::get_cycles(), so a difference is the
# inversion changing behaviour, which is exactly what must not happen.
#
# Skips (77) rather than fails when a binary or the platform file is absent: an
# environment without a FastSim build has nothing to say about S1.
set -uo pipefail

NAME=cycle_mode_on_lua
ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_matmul}"
ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$ROOT/tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-300}"

skip() { echo "[skip] $NAME: $*"; exit 77; }
fail() { echo "FAIL[$NAME]: $*"; exit 1; }

VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
[ -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]           || skip "vsim engine not built: $VSIM_BIN"
[ -f "$ELF" ]                || skip "fixture ELF not built: $ELF"
[ -n "${FASTSIM_BIN:-}" ]    || skip "FASTSIM_BIN unset (multi_arch_toplevel)"
[ -x "${FASTSIM_BIN}" ]      || skip "FastSim not built: $FASTSIM_BIN"
[ -n "${VSIM_CYCLE_LUA:-}" ] || skip "VSIM_CYCLE_LUA unset (cycle-mode platform)"
[ -f "${VSIM_CYCLE_LUA}" ]   || skip "Lua platform missing: $VSIM_CYCLE_LUA"
[ -n "${VSIM_CORE_SO:-}" ]   || skip "VSIM_CORE_SO unset (VsimCore .so, no suffix)"
[ -f "${VSIM_CORE_SO}.so" ]  || skip "VsimCore not built: ${VSIM_CORE_SO}.so"

# Lift the one number vsim reports. Shared by both legs on purpose: if the legs
# scraped differently, a formatting change could hide a real move.
cycles_from() {
  sed -nE 's/.*[^0-9]([0-9]+) cycles simulated.*/\1/p' | tail -1
}

# -- leg 1: vsim owns the kernel (today) --------------------------------------
A_OUT=$(timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$ELF" 2>&1); A_RC=$?
A=$(printf '%s\n' "$A_OUT" | cycles_from)
[ -n "$A" ] || fail "vsim standalone reported no cycle count (rc=$A_RC)
$(printf '%s\n' "$A_OUT" | tail -5)"

# -- leg 2: FastSim owns the kernel (S1) --------------------------------------
# multi_arch_toplevel takes no parameter flags -- the platform file IS the
# interface. So layer the two per-run facts over the committed platform with
# dofile() instead of duplicating it, which would let the two drift apart.
WORK=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/$NAME.XXXXXX") || fail "mktemp failed"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
cat > "$WORK/run.lua" <<LUA
dofile("$VSIM_CYCLE_LUA")
platform.vsim.elf_file = "$ELF"
platform.vsim.dylib_path = "$VSIM_CORE_SO"
LUA

B_OUT=$(cd "$WORK" && timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$FASTSIM_BIN" --gs_luafile "$WORK/run.lua" 2>&1); B_RC=$?
B=$(printf '%s\n' "$B_OUT" | cycles_from)
[ -n "$B" ] || fail "FastSim-hosted run reported no cycle count (rc=$B_RC)
$(printf '%s\n' "$B_OUT" | tail -20)"

# -- the contract -------------------------------------------------------------
if [ "$A" != "$B" ]; then
  fail "cycle count moved when FastSim took the kernel:
  vsim standalone (sc_start per cycle): $A
  FastSim + Lua   (wait per cycle):     $B
  moved by $((B - A)) cycles on fixture $FIXTURE"
fi

echo "[$NAME] PASS: $FIXTURE = $A cycles, both ways"
SH

echo "=== RUN ==="
VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build \
FASTSIM_BIN="$SP"/fsbuild/multi_arch_toplevel \
VSIM_CYCLE_LUA=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/conf/andesim_cycle_ax45mpv_premium.lua \
VSIM_CORE_SO=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/VsimCore_ax45mpv_premium \
